recipes.title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
recipes.description: The Roman classic: eggs, cured pork and pecorino emulsified into a glossy sauce. No cream, ever.
ingredients: 150 g guanciale, cut into short batons
Coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil and drop in the spaghetti.
Render the guanciale in a cold, dry pan over medium heat until the fat runs clear and the edges crisp, about 8 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, yolk, pecorino and a heavy grind of black pepper into a thick paste.
Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti one minute short of the packet time.
Toss the pasta through the guanciale off the heat, then stir in the egg mixture, loosening with pasta water until the sauce coats every strand.
Serve immediately with extra pecorino and pepper.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.description: Tall, tangy pancakes with a tender crumb. The batter wants to rest before it hits the pan.
ingredients: Half a tsp bicarbonate of soda
50 g butter, melted, plus more for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in a large bowl.
In a second bowl beat the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter until smooth.
Fold the wet into the dry with a few strokes only - lumps are fine, overmixing is not.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes while a heavy pan heats over medium-low.
Butter the pan and ladle in the batter. Flip when the surface bubbles and the edges look set, roughly 2 minutes.
Cook a further minute and keep warm in a low oven while you finish the batch.

recipes.title: Roasted Tomato Soup
recipes.description: Roasting concentrates the tomatoes before they ever meet the blender, so the soup tastes of far more than its six ingredients.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C. Spread the tomatoes, onion and garlic on a large tray.
Coat with the olive oil, season generously and roast for 40 minutes until the edges char.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and tip everything, including the tray juices, into a saucepan.
Add the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir the basil through and adjust the seasoning.
Loosen with a little more stock if the soup is thicker than you like.

recipes.title: Classic Caesar Salad
recipes.description: Cos lettuce, an anchovy-backed dressing and croutons fried in the same pan. Assemble at the last moment.
ingredients: 2 heads of cos lettuce, leaves separated
2 thick slices of sourdough, torn into chunks
steps: Fry the torn sourdough in olive oil over medium heat until golden on all sides, then drain on paper.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste with the flat of a knife.
Whisk the paste with the egg yolk, mustard and lemon juice.
Trickle in the olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing thickens to double cream.
Toss the lettuce through the dressing so every leaf is lightly coated.
Scatter over the croutons and shaved parmesan and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies
recipes.description: Dense and fudgy rather than cakey. Pull them out while the middle still has a wobble.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together over a pan of barely simmering water, then let the mixture cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the sugar, eggs and vanilla until pale and thickened, about 3 minutes.
Fold the chocolate mixture in, then sift over the flour, cocoa and salt and fold until just combined.
Spread into the tin and bake for 25 minutes - the centre should still wobble slightly.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 squares.

recipes.title: Fresh Guacamole
recipes.description: Chunky rather than smooth, built in the bowl you serve it in. Lime keeps the colour honest.
ingredients: Half a red onion, finely diced
steps: Halve the avocados, scoop the flesh into a bowl and add the lime juice straight away.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving plenty of texture.
Stir through the onion, chilli and coriander.
Fold in the diced tomato last so it stays intact.
Season with sea salt, taste, and add more lime if it needs lifting.
Serve within the hour with warm tortilla chips.

recipes.title: Smoky Shakshuka
recipes.description: Eggs baked in a warmly spiced tomato and pepper sauce, finished with herbs and crusty bread.
ingredients: A handful of parsley or coriander
steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide lidded pan and cook the onion and pepper with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 to 8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Scatter over herbs and serve with bread for scooping.

recipes.title: Silky Lemon Hummus
recipes.description: A smooth, bright chickpea dip with plenty of tahini, lemon and a pool of olive oil.
ingredients: Salt and warm flatbreads to serve
steps: Blend the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Add the chickpeas and blend, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, add the cold water a spoonful at a time until the hummus is pale and silky.
Taste and adjust with more lemon or salt.
Spoon into a shallow bowl, make a well in the centre and finish with olive oil.
Serve with warm flatbreads or crisp vegetables.

recipes.title: Herby Lentil Soup
recipes.description: A satisfying one-pot soup of green lentils, vegetables and lemon, made for weekday lunches.
steps: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the olive oil with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and lentils and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, add the bay leaves and bring to a boil.
Lower to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Remove the bay leaves and season with lemon zest, juice, salt and pepper.
Serve with parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.title: Miso Salmon Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Glazed salmon, steamed rice and crunchy cucumber brought together with a quick miso dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the miso, soy sauce, honey and sesame oil, then brush it over the salmon.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and the glaze is caramelised.
Warm the rice and divide it between two bowls.
Top with cucumber, salmon and spring onions.
Finish with sesame seeds and lime.

recipes.title: Crispy Roast Potatoes
recipes.description: Craggy, golden potatoes with a fluffy centre and rosemary-scented edges.
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
4 tbsp olive oil or goose fat
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C and put a roasting tray with the oil inside to heat.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, then drain well.
Shake the potatoes in the colander to rough up the edges.
Carefully add them to the hot fat with the garlic and rosemary and turn to coat.
Roast for 45 minutes, turning twice, until deeply golden and crisp.
Season with flaky salt and pepper before serving.

recipes.title: Summer Berry Crumble
recipes.description: Juicy berries under a buttery oat topping that stays crisp around the edges.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 C and place the berries in a baking dish.
Toss the berries with the caster sugar and cornflour.
Rub the flour, oats, butter, brown sugar and salt together until coarse crumbs form.
Scatter the crumble evenly over the fruit.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve warm with yoghurt or ice cream.

recipes.title: Vanilla Iced Coffee
recipes.description: Cold-brew-style coffee over ice with a hint of vanilla and a silky splash of milk.
ingredients: 2 tsp maple syrup or sugar syrup
steps: Stir the chilled coffee, maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon together.
Fill two tall glasses generously with ice.
Pour the coffee over the ice.
Top with milk and stir gently.
Taste and add another splash of syrup if desired.
